arguments.summary: Final research draft: all five instruments remain insufficient_evidence for the 21/63-session mandate. Dated operating and technical context is differentiated, but critical gaps in issuer valuation/forward evidence, current QQQ composition, and/or quantified policy exposure prevent directional conclusions or rankings.

claims.text: ANET reported $5.7447bn six-month revenue through June 30, 2026 and outperformed SPY by 7.90 percentage points over 21 sessions and 15.51 points over 63 sessions through September 18.

QQQ's sponsor profile reported aggregate P/E of 30.08 as of August 31, 2026; its September 12 holdings file is stale and listed NVDA at 8.45%, MU at 4.85%, META at 3.07%, and top-10 holdings at 47.17%.
MU reported $78.959bn nine-month revenue through May 28, 2026; its 21-session return was 8.40%, versus -10.42% over 63 sessions, and 63-session realized volatility was 89.56%.
META reported $64.088bn six-month operating cash flow and $49.113bn capital expenditure through June 30, 2026; it exceeded SPY by 22.88 percentage points over 21 sessions and XLC by 22.38 points.

NVDA reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $96.2bn and guided Q3 revenue to $108.0bn plus or minus 2%, assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China; its September 18 close was above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs.
On September 16, 2026, the FOMC raised the target federal-funds range to 3.75%–4.00% and described inflation as elevated alongside solid activity and robust capital investment.

The evidence differentiates descriptive market context—ANET and META relative strength, MU's volatile recovery after 63-session weakness, QQQ's weaker 63-session relative performance, and NVDA's stated reporting catalyst—but does not establish forward returns.

Elevated rates may pressure technology multiples while robust capital investment may support AI-infrastructure demand; a relevant trade-policy action could affect shipments, supply, demand, or compliance. Magnitude and issuer-level transmission are unquantified.

gaps.description: No market-derived issuer valuation baseline or sufficient verified forward earnings/guidance evidence for ANET prevents a near-horizon valuation assessment.
QQQ's supplied holdings snapshot is stale, preventing a current constituent look-through conclusion.
MU's current cycle, pricing, supply, inventory and guidance evidence was not verified, and no market-derived issuer valuation baseline is supplied.
META's provided materials lack verified guidance, advertising-demand detail and AI-spending/monetization disclosure, and no market-derived issuer valuation baseline is supplied.
No complete quantified direct trade-policy exposure mapping or market-derived issuer valuation baseline is available for NVDA.
No dated primary policy text maps current covered products, jurisdictions or counterparties to issuer financial exposure.

assumptions: Price returns, volatility, RSI and moving averages are descriptive completed-session observations, not forecasts.
Company reporting periods differ and are not directly comparable.
QQQ weights are dated fund composition only, not current exposure or a personalized allocation.
Rates/capex and trade-policy mechanisms are conditional scenarios, not measured issuer sensitivities.
arguments.counter_thesis: Reported profitability, cash generation, constructive moving-average posture and NVDA's explicit outlook could support resilience. However, missing valuation and forward-operating inputs mean that strength may already be reflected; stale QQQ holdings and unquantified direct policy exposure preclude exposure-based conclusions.

review_conditions.description: Review after current issuer materials establish valuation inputs, forward guidance and demand/supply or monetization evidence, and after primary policy material maps any restriction to issuer exposure.
Refresh sponsor holdings before relying on QQQ constituent look-through.
